function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools and platforms you can use to book flights—whether you’re looking for a simple web interface, a mobile app, or an API you can integrate into your own software.

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Web & Mobile Booking Platforms** | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price alerts, flexible date grids | Quick price comparison, exploring routes |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregates many airlines, price alerts, “Price Forecast” | Budget planning, multi‑city itineraries |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global coverage, “Everywhere” search, price alerts | Finding cheapest destinations, flexible travel |
| | **Expedia** | Bundles flights + hotels + car rentals | One‑stop booking for trips |
| | **Priceline** | “Name Your Own Price” and “Express Deals” | Last‑minute deals, budget travelers |
| | **Orbitz** | Loyalty program, “Orbitz Rewards” | Frequent travelers who want points |
| | **Momondo** | Transparent fare breakdown, “Price Insight” | Understanding fare components |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia, multi‑currency | International travelers, Asian routes |
| | **CheapOair** | Promo codes, “Price Match” | Discount seekers, coupon users |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Expedia, often bundled offers | One‑stop booking, family trips |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” for last‑minute flights | Quick bookings, last‑minute travelers |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** (for flight + experience bundles) | Bundled experiences | Travelers wanting curated trips |
| | **Airline Websites** (e.g., Delta, United, Emirates) | Direct booking, loyalty points | Frequent flyers, brand loyalty |
| | **Mobile Apps** (e.g., Hopper, Skyscanner, Google Flights) | Price predictions, push alerts | On‑the‑go travelers, price monitoring |
| **API & SDK Solutions** | **Skyscanner API** | Search flights, price alerts, multi‑city | Developers building travel apps |
| | **Google Flights API** (via Google Travel) | Flight search, price history | Integrating flight data into services |
| | **Amadeus Travel API** | Comprehensive flight data, booking, seat selection | Enterprise travel tech, OTA solutions |

You can choose the one that best fits your needs (e.g., real‑time flight tracking vs. flight search vs. booking).

---

### How to Pick the Right Tool

| Need | Recommended Tool | Why |
|------|------------------|-----|
| **Quick price comparison** | Google Flights, Skyscanner, Kayak | Fast, no sign‑up required |
| **Last‑minute deals** | Hotwire, Priceline, Expedia | “Express Deals” or “Name Your Own Price” |
| **Bundle flights + hotels** | Expedia, Orbitz, Travelocity | One‑stop booking, loyalty points |
| **Frequent flyer loyalty** | Airline direct sites (Delta, United, Emirates) | Earn miles, manage status |
| **Developer integration** | Skyscanner API, Amadeus API, Sabre API | Build custom booking flows |
| **Real‑time flight status** | FlightAware API, FlightRadar24 API | Track delays, gate changes |
| **Multi‑city itineraries** | Kiwi.com API, Skyscanner API | Complex routing, low‑cost carriers |
| **Budget travel** | CheapOair, Hopper | Promo codes, price predictions |
| **International focus** | Trip.com, Skyscanner | Multi‑currency, global coverage |

---

### Quick Tips

1. **Use price alerts** – Most aggregators let you set alerts for specific routes. This is great if you’re flexible on dates.
2. **Check airline direct sites** – Sometimes airlines offer exclusive fares or better seat selection options.
3. **Leverage loyalty programs** – If you’re a frequent flyer, booking directly can earn you miles or status upgrades.
4. **Consider bundling** – If you’re also booking hotels or cars, an OTA (online travel agency) can sometimes give you a discount.
5. **Watch for hidden fees** – Some aggregators add extra charges for baggage or seat selection. Check the fine print before you finalize.

---

### Bottom Line

- **For casual travelers**: Google Flights, Skyscanner, Kayak, or Expedia are your best bets.
- **For frequent flyers**: Book directly with airlines or use loyalty‑focused platforms like Orbitz or Expedia.
- **For developers**: Skyscanner API, Amadeus API, or Sabre API give you the flexibility to build custom booking experiences.
- **For real‑time flight tracking**: FlightAware or FlightRadar24 APIs are industry standards.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any specific platform, or if you’re looking for a particular type of booking (e.g., corporate, group, or last‑minute). Happy travels!
